Messages.Author: brettscho
Messages.Body:
> Maddog wrote:
> Regarding TWDA site, what ever happened to the option of being able to search by Clans?
> Is there any plans to bring that back.
>
While the TWDA archive isn't currently separated by clan, I've created a google document that does (although I've only gone through decks 2008 to the present). It also includes a fair amount of useful statistics like which crypt groupings are the most popular, how many people attended each event (and how many attend all events in a single year), things like that. It always provides a link back to the deck, so you can just find the clan you are most interested in, and click on decks to be taken to their entry in TWDA. You can get access to that  google doc here . I try to publicize it in my sig, but I think a lot of people don't know that it exists.

Oh, and the definition I used (shamelessly stolen from ICL) is that the crypt must be comprised of >50% one clan, and it must have at least 2 crypt cards from that clan. It's not a perfect definition, but seems to work pretty well.

Check out my VTES blog:  Gaming with BS

Messages.Author: BenPeal
Messages.Body:
> brettscho wrote:
> Oh, and the definition I used (shamelessly stolen from ICL) is that the crypt must be comprised of >50% one clan, and it must have at least 2 crypt cards from that clan. It's not a perfect definition, but seems to work pretty well.
>
Yeah, seems decent. It covers the distinction between a "clan deck" and a "star player deck". It also accounts for Anarch decks that use Anarch Converts such that they're not considered Caitiff decks (unless other Caitiff are used). Tupdog decks wouldn't be considered Gargoyle decks in this scheme.

A question to consider is how people use the TWDA-by-clan. Are they mainly looking for "clan decks" or are they looking for "something I can do with this clan"? If it's the former, then the ICL-brettscho approach would be preferable. If it's the latter, Lasombra Jeff's approach would be preferable.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
For the league of Paris, we have the following rule:

- if a clan has more copies that any other clan, it's considered to be of that clan
- if there's a tie, we consider the clan of the "star" vampire, that is a vampire who has more copies than any other
- if there's again a tie, we consider the clan of the vampire with the highest capacity
- if there's still a tie, well, it's random.

So:
- a Tupdog deck would be considered to be a Gargoyle deck (after, you'll play mainly with them).
- a deck wih plenty of Anarch Converts could erroneously be considered to be Caitiff (Caitiff is a clan for that matter).
- a  turbo baron deck would be considered to be Giovanni (assuming you play more Giovannis than any other clan)

That's the limits. Otherwise, this system works fine too.

Prince of Paris, France
